chunks: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Tamim al-Sarakhsi, the Jurist, in it, said: Abu Lubaid Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shami narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muhajir al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hariri narrated to me, from Abu'l-Ward ibn Tamama, from Al-Lajlaj, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, saying:

I was with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), and a man passed by whilst saying: 'O Allah, I ask You for patience.' Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) said to him: 'You have asked for affliction, so ask Allah for comfort (well-being).' He (peace be upon him and his Family) also passed by a man whilst he was saying: 'O Allah, I ask You for the perfection of the grace.' Then he said: 'O Son of Adam, and do you know what the perfection of the grace is? It is Salvation from the Fire and entrance to Paradise.' He (peace be upon him and his Family) passed by a man whilst he was praying and saying: 'O the One of Glory and Generosity.' Then he said to him: 'It has been responded to you, so ask.'

key_terms.ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَام: The One of Glory and Generosity (Divine Attribute)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between asking for patience and asking for well-being in Islamic supplication?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to elucidate the theological nuance between enduring hardship and seeking divine protection, a key theme in Shia supplicatory tradition. The Prophet’s guidance distinguishes between the passive endurance of trials ('patience') and the active preservation of health and faith ('well-being'), while defining ultimate success not merely as worldly blessing but as eschatological salvation. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *'afiyah* as a comprehensive state of physical, spiritual, and worldly integrity.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Abu Nasr, Muhammed bin Ahmad bin Tamim al-Sarakhsi, the Jurist, in it [1], that he said: We were told by Abu Lubaid, Muhammed bin Idrees al-Shami, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Muhajir al-Baghdadi, that he said: We were told by Isma’eel bin Ibrahim, that he said: I was told by Hareeri, from Abu’l-Ward bin Tamama, from Lajlaj, from Mu’adh bin Jabal, that he said:

I was with the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and a man passed by whilst saying: «O Allah, I ask You for patience». Then the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: You have asked for affliction, so ask Allah for comfort. He, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, also passed by whilst he was saying: «O Allah, I ask you for the perfection of the grace.» Then he said: (O) Son of Adam, and do you know what the perfection of the grace is? (It is) Salvation from the Fire and entrance to Paradise. He, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, passed by a man whilst he was praying and saying: «O the One of Glory and Generosity». Then he said to him: «It has been responded to you, so ask.»
